issues.where: upper right sky above the limb (frames 4956-4967, starting in sheet-04 frames 4933-4949 and continuing in sheet-05 frames 4950-4963)
issues.what: the right edge of the terrain sky picture slides roughly 85 pixels into frame, exposing a stark vertical cutoff to black while cross-dissolving into a shifted 3D starfield
issues.fix: extend or seamlessly wrap the terrain sky plate well past the full pan/pullback frustum and lock its orientation and motion to the 3D skybox

issues.where: planet storm surface and upper left of the vortex (frames 4712-4745)
issues.what: without an opaque cloud cover masking the dive handoff, the 3D globe storm texture cross-dissolves directly into a finite sphere-projected terrain decal, producing a ghosted double-exposure of both storm systems at frame 4720, a hard dark-navy patch drop-off above-left of the spiral, truncated ends on the diagonal cumulus ridge, and a lingering white globe cloud patch on the right edge at 4729 that vanishes by 4737
issues.fix: pass camera through an opaque cloud/haze cover during the dive swap or blend multi-resolution planet textures seamlessly so neither double-exposed storms nor finite decal borders appear

issues.where: planet surface around the spiral vortex and diagonal cumulus band (frames 4970-4997)
issues.what: during the rise pullback, the finite terrain decal shrinks in open view on the globe—exposing both abruptly cut-off ends of the straight cumulus ridge and the dark-navy decal boundary above-left of the eye (4970-4984)—before visibly cross-dissolving as a ghosted double-exposure back into the 3D globe storm texture (4984-4990)
issues.fix: complete the terrain-to-globe transition inside an opaque atmospheric/cloud cover before pulling the camera wide enough to reveal the terrain patch edges

issues.where: foreground diagonal cumulus ridge and far upper-right horizon cloud band (frames 4819-4949)
issues.what: unreset 2D UV flow advection progressively stretches and smears the crisp cumulus puffs into stringy, taffy-like fibrous streaks and concentric arcs while shearing and tearing apart the thin white cloud line along the upper-right horizon
issues.fix: use dual-phase regenerating flow-map cycling or layered 3D cloud cards with bounded displacement so cloud flow and depth parallax never stretch or tear the texture

issues.where: upper-right starfield and upper-left cloud deck across the dive cover (frames 4747-4758)
issues.what: frames across the nominal dive cover are an open cross-dissolve rather than a continuous covered move: a 3D Milky Way drifting down-right double-exposes over a misaligned 2D Milky Way plate drifting up-left (with a narrow dark cutoff strip at the far right edge in 4755-4758), while the dark-navy sphere-decal boundary on the upper left fades out into the brighter 2.5D cloud deck
issues.fix: match skyfield coordinates and motion across the handoff and mask the 3D-to-terrain switch inside a genuine atmospheric cloud cover

issues.where: left cloud deck and upper-left cumulus ridge across the rise cover (frames 4956-4967)
issues.what: cross-fading from the 2.5D terrain view back to the finite sphere decal without a cover rapidly darkens the left side of the frame (mean luminance drops ~16% over 11 frames) as the dark-navy decal border fades in and clips off the upper-left cumulus clouds
issues.fix: match color and extent beyond the left frustum edge or obscure the handoff inside an atmospheric cloud cover so exposure and cloud continuity hold across the move

issues.where: fast pullback across planet limb, rings, and stars (frames 4970-5011, and dive frames 4696-4720 in sheet-02.png)
issues.what: high-speed plunge and pullback frames have no motion blur, leaving rapidly whipping stars, cloud edges, and fine ring arcs frozen sharp with stair-stepped aliasing along the rings
issues.fix: enable smooth shutter/camera motion blur proportional to screen-space velocity and filter thin ring structures to prevent aliasing shimmer

issues.what: the moon's surface texture rotates roughly 60 degrees on its axis over 150 frames while advancing only slightly along its orbit, spinning unrealistically fast compared to the planet
issues.fix: slow the moon's axial rotation to a believable tidally locked or slow sidereal rate consistent with its orbital speed
